examples.suggested: maklumkan kepada moderator

editor_note: Overall the translation is faithful and uses "mitigasi ralat", "litar templat", "hingar" and "model pelaksanaan terarah" consistently. examples.suggested: anda boleh menentukan lapisan mana dalam litar yang hendak dimitigasi

editor_note: In entry [7], "conjugate transpose" is translated as "anak matrik konjugat". In Malay mathematics "anak matriks" means a submatrix or minor, so a learner would come away thinking the inverse gate is a conjugate submatrix instead of "transpos konjugat". This wrong term is the reason for the FAIL. The other problems are minor calques: "Dalam kata-kata" for "In words" [25], "dengan kepastian" for "with certainty" [11], "bit klasik ... sentiasa bersetuju" for bits that "agree" (better "sepadan") [51], "secara berkesan" for "effectively" [21, 31], and "85% daripada masa" [66]. Everything else is faithful, and the core terms are consistent (litar, get, jalinan, qubit, pengekodan superpadu).

examples.why: 'Anak matriks' means submatrix/minor, which gives a false definition of the inverse of a unitary. The standard term is 'transpos konjugat'.

editor_note: Entry [203] reverses the meaning of the English. It renders "neither the swap operation nor the controlled-NOT operation ... can be expressed as a tensor product" as "baik operasi swap mahupun operasi controlled-NOT ... boleh dinyatakan". Without "tidak", that tells the learner both operations CAN be written as tensor products, which is the opposite of the point being taught. There are also smaller problems. "Proper subset" is calqued as "subset yang betul" ("correct subset") in [72], [114], [126] and [193], where the standard math term is "subset wajar". [165] uses "memesan" (to order, as in purchase) for ordering elements instead of "menyusun". [110] and [160] have the awkward double copula "adalah 1 ialah", and [158] renders "conditioned upon" as "bergantung pada".

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. Probability-vector conditions, stochastic-matrix properties, M2M1 composition order and the non-commutativity caveat are all intact, and core terms are consistent (keadaan kebarangkalian, vektor asas piawai, matriks stokastik, bersekutu, kalis tukar tertib). A native editor would still fix a few stiff calques and grammar slips. These are "infiniti banyak" for "infinitely many" in [8], "Persamaan ini mengikut fakta" for "follows from" in [88], the incomplete "muncul bilangan yang sama" in [46] and the dangling "yang akan kita kembali" in [7]. "Composing" becomes "menggabungkan" even though the heading and tooltip use "Komposisi", and "penerangan matematik mereka" in [3] uses "mereka" for a non-human referent.

examples.source: physical systems having *infinitely* many classical states
examples.translation: sistem fizikal yang mempunyai *infiniti* banyak keadaan klasikal
examples.suggested: sistem fizikal yang mempunyai keadaan klasikal yang *tak terhingga* banyaknya
examples.why: "infiniti banyak" copies the English word for word. The normal Malay mathematical phrasing is "tak terhingga banyaknya", which also matches "terhingga" (finite) used earlier in the same paragraph.

examples.source: The equality follows from the fact that matrix multiplication ... is an associative operation.
examples.translation: Persamaan ini mengikut fakta bahawa pendaraban matriks ...
examples.suggested: Kesamaan ini terhasil daripada fakta bahawa pendaraban matriks ...
examples.why: In this sentence "mengikut" reads as 'according to' rather than the logical 'follows from'. "terhasil daripada" or "diperoleh daripada" is the idiomatic way to say it in a proof.

examples.source: each of the two output values occurs the same number of times
examples.translation: setiap daripada dua nilai output muncul bilangan yang sama
examples.suggested: setiap satu daripada dua nilai output muncul sebanyak bilangan kali yang sama
examples.why: "kali" (times) and a linking word are missing, so the sentence is ungrammatical even though the meaning can still be recovered.

examples.source: The archetypal example, which we will come back to repeatedly
examples.translation: Contoh yang paling asas, yang akan kita kembali berulang kali
examples.suggested: Contoh utama, yang akan kita rujuk semula berulang kali
examples.why: "kembali" needs a complement ("kembali kepadanya"). As written, the relative clause is incomplete.

examples.source: obtained by composing the first and second probabilistic operations
examples.translation: diperoleh dengan menggabungkan operasi kebarangkalian pertama dan kedua
examples.suggested: diperoleh dengan mengkomposisikan (menggubah) operasi kebarangkalian pertama dan kedua
examples.why: The section heading and tooltip use "Komposisi", but the verb becomes "menggabungkan" (combine), which loosens the link to the technical notion of sequential composition. The same rendering appears in [89] and [95].

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the unitary/stochastic/permutation claims, the Born rule and the H|+>=|0> distinguishability argument, so nothing here would mislead a learner. Several passages are calqued from English: "Dalam kata-kata" (In words), "Dalam nada yang sama" (Along similar lines), "sejauh pengukuran asas piawai berkenaan", "Mengapa, kemudiannya", and the cleft "ia adalah hasil tambah ... yang mesti". There are also some word-choice slips. "Speedup" is rendered "kelajuan" (speed) rather than "pecutan/percepatan". Transpose is split between "transpos" and "dipindah urus". "Imaginer" is Indonesian rather than Malay "khayalan". "Mengkuasakan" should be "mengkuasaduakan" for squaring. "Ia mungkin secara prinsipnya" reads as "it is perhaps in principle".

examples.source: any speedup from a quantum computer
examples.translation: mana-mana kelajuan dari komputer kuantum
examples.suggested: sebarang pecutan (speedup) yang diperoleh daripada komputer kuantum
examples.why: 'kelajuan' means speed, not the computational speedup (advantage) the source means.

examples.source: where the vector is transposed from a column vector to a row vector
examples.translation: di mana vektor dipindah urus daripada vektor lajur kepada vektor baris
examples.suggested: di mana vektor ditranspos daripada vektor lajur kepada vektor baris
examples.why: The same sentence uses 'transpos konjugat', so 'dipindah urus' for the verb is inconsistent and not a common term. [83] repeats it.

examples.source: In words, this is a *uniform superposition*
examples.translation: Dalam kata-kata, ini adalah *superposisi seragam*
examples.suggested: Dengan kata lain, ini ialah *superposisi seragam*
examples.why: 'Dalam kata-kata' is a word-for-word calque, and a native writer would say 'Dengan kata lain'.

examples.source: but it is possible in principle
examples.translation: tetapi ia mungkin secara prinsipnya
examples.suggested: tetapi secara prinsipnya ia boleh dilakukan
examples.why: 'ia mungkin' reads as 'it is perhaps', which blurs the claim that this is possible in principle.

examples.source: as far as standard basis measurements are concerned ... Why, then, would we care
examples.translation: sejauh pengukuran asas piawai berkenaan ... Mengapa, kemudiannya, kita perlu
examples.suggested: dari segi pengukuran asas piawai ... Jadi, mengapa kita perlu
examples.why: Both phrases copy English syntax, and 'kemudiannya' means 'afterwards', not the inferential 'then'.

examples.source: the imaginary part of these numbers
examples.translation: bahagian imaginer nombor-nombor ini
examples.suggested: bahagian khayalan nombor-nombor ini
examples.why: 'imaginer' is Indonesian usage, and standard Malay mathematics uses 'khayalan'.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner, but a native editor would change several word choices. In [23], "piloting solutions" became "mempercontohi penyelesaian", which means "to exemplify" rather than "to run a pilot"; "merintis" would be right. In [29], "virtuous cycle" is calqued as "kitaran berbudi"; "kitaran positif" is the natural Malay phrase. Other slips: "Ramai yang beroperasi" in [25] uses "ramai", a word for people, for organisations; "kekangan mereka" in [6] uses "mereka" for inanimate deliverables; and Indonesian-leaning "terobosan" and "dunia nyata" appear in [19], [22] and [23] where Malay would use "kejayaan besar" and "dunia sebenar".

examples.source: piloting solutions that demonstrate measurable impact
examples.translation: mempercontohi penyelesaian yang menunjukkan impak
examples.suggested: merintis penyelesaian yang menunjukkan impak
examples.why: 'mempercontohi' means to exemplify or model, not to run a pilot or trial.

examples.source: this virtuous cycle of open education and open-source development
examples.translation: kitaran berbudi ini antara pendidikan terbuka dan pembangunan sumber terbuka
examples.suggested: kitaran positif antara pendidikan terbuka dan pembangunan sumber terbuka ini
examples.why: 'berbudi' (kind or virtuous as a personal trait) is a literal calque; the idiom in Malay is 'kitaran positif'.

examples.source: Many operate as a hub
examples.translation: Ramai yang beroperasi sebagai hab
examples.suggested: Kebanyakannya beroperasi sebagai hab
examples.why: 'Ramai' is used for people; the referent here is centres or organisations.

examples.source: realistic deliverables and their constraints
examples.translation: hasil yang realistik dan kekangan mereka
examples.suggested: hasil yang realistik serta kekangannya
examples.why: 'mereka' refers to people; for inanimate things Malay uses the suffix '-nya'.

examples.source: accelerating technical breakthroughs ... real-world applications
examples.translation: mempercepatkan terobosan teknikal ... aplikasi dunia nyata
examples.suggested: mempercepatkan kejayaan besar teknikal ... aplikasi dunia sebenar
examples.why: 'terobosan' and 'dunia nyata' lean Indonesian; standard Malay prefers 'kejayaan besar' and 'dunia sebenar'.

editor_note: The translation is faithful overall. It is not misleading: the parity reasoning, the two loop categories, the distance-L argument and the [[2L^2,2,L]] count all survive intact. "Multiply" appears two ways. [28] and [45] correctly use "darabkan", but [45], [48] and [53] also use "menggandakan", which in Malay usually means "to double". The closing sentence of [67] loses the direction of the error-rate change ("decreases past" became "melepasi"). "Fixed by all stabilizer generators" in [31] became "ditetapkan oleh", which reads as "set/determined by", not "left unchanged by". Smaller points: [48] drops "effectively" and changes "shrunk to the identity" to "dikecutkan menjadi tiada" ("shrunk to nothing"), and [52] calls the loop "rantaian" ("chain") where the English says "loop".

examples.source: can be obtained by multiplying together the $X$ stabilizer generators
examples.translation: boleh diperoleh dengan menggandakan penjana penstabilan $X$
examples.suggested: boleh diperoleh dengan mendarabkan bersama penjana penstabilan $X$
examples.why: 'menggandakan' usually means 'to double' and clashes with 'darabkan' used earlier in [28] and in [45] itself; the same slip recurs in [48] and [53].

examples.source: a faster decrease in the probability for a logical error as the error rate decreases past the break-even point
examples.translation: penurunan yang lebih pantas dalam kebarangkalian ralat logik apabila kadar ralat melepasi titik impas
examples.suggested: ... apabila kadar ralat menurun melepasi titik impas
examples.why: The direction is lost ('decreases past' became 'passes'), so the sentence no longer says the benefit applies below the threshold.

examples.source: at least one quantum state vector is fixed by all of the stabilizer generators
examples.translation: sekurang-kurangnya satu vektor keadaan kuantum ditetapkan oleh semua penjana penstabilan
examples.suggested: sekurang-kurangnya satu vektor keadaan kuantum kekal tidak berubah di bawah semua penjana penstabilan
examples.why: 'ditetapkan oleh' reads as 'set/determined by' rather than 'left invariant by'.

examples.source: they can effectively be shrunk to the identity by multiplying them by $X$ stabilizer generators
examples.translation: ia boleh dikecutkan menjadi tiada dengan menggandakannya dengan penjana penstabilan $X$
examples.suggested: ia boleh dikecutkan kepada operasi identiti dengan mendarabkannya dengan penjana penstabilan $X$
examples.why: Drops 'effectively' and replaces 'identity' with 'nothing', and again uses 'menggandakan' for 'multiplying'.

editor_note: Entry [41] reverses the substitution in the Shor-code explanation. The English means X⊗X⊗X takes the place of X, but "X⊗X⊗X digantikan dengan X" says X⊗X⊗X is replaced by X, so a learner would read the stabilizer construction backwards. There are also smaller slips. "Kod ulangan" becomes "kod repetisi" in [123]. "Takrifan/mentakrifkan" is mixed with "definisi/didefinisikan" in [89] and [149]. The Indonesian "diklaim" appears in [140], and there are calques: "finit banyak" in [100], "boleh membolehkan" in [52], "dengan cara" for "by the way" in [111], and "model bunyi" for noise model (conventionally "model hingar") in [147].

examples.source: except that $X\otimes X\otimes X$ is substituted for $X$
examples.translation: kecuali $X\otimes X\otimes X$ digantikan dengan $X$
examples.suggested: kecuali $X$ digantikan dengan $X\otimes X\otimes X$
examples.why: The direction of the replacement is reversed. The Malay says X⊗X⊗X is swapped out for X, but the source says the opposite, which is what explains the form of the last two Shor stabilizer generators.

examples.source: for the 3-bit repetition code
examples.translation: untuk kod repetisi 3-bit
examples.suggested: untuk kod ulangan 3-bit
examples.why: Everywhere else in the file the term is 'kod ulangan'. Switching to 'repetisi' here makes it inconsistent.

examples.source: as claimed
examples.translation: seperti yang diklaim
examples.suggested: seperti yang dinyatakan / seperti yang didakwa
examples.why: 'Diklaim' is Indonesian. Entry [81] already uses the Malay 'dituntut'.

examples.source: there are only *finitely* many $n$-qubit Clifford operations
examples.translation: hanya terdapat *finit* banyak operasi Clifford
examples.suggested: hanya terdapat bilangan *terhingga* operasi Clifford
examples.why: 'Finit banyak' is a word-for-word calque of 'finitely many'. The standard Malay is 'bilangan terhingga'.

examples.source: for some noise models
examples.translation: untuk sesetengah model bunyi
examples.suggested: untuk sesetengah model hingar
examples.why: Here 'noise' means signal or physical noise, which Malay technical writing calls 'hingar'. 'Bunyi' means acoustic sound.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and the core terms are used consistently: superposisi seragam, pantulan/putaran, dijangkau oleh, fasa global. Nothing would mislead a learner, but several phrases read as calques. In [9], "set yang bersamaannya" ("its equal set") should be "set yang sepadan", and "A_0 mahupun A_1 tidak kosong" is less clear than "kedua-dua A_0 dan A_1 tidak kosong". In [36], "ungkapan ini bersetuju dengan definisi" copies English "agrees with". In [81] and [85], "pantulan tentang garis" copies "reflection about the line" and should use "terhadap". [2] also has a spelling error: "menvisualisasikan" should be "memvisualisasikan".

examples.source: each of these vectors is only defined when its corresponding set is nonempty, but hereafter we're going to focus on the case that neither $A_0$ nor $A_1$ is empty
examples.translation: setiap vektor ini hanya ditakrifkan apabila set yang bersamaannya tidak kosong, tetapi mulai sekarang kita akan fokus pada kes di mana $A_0$ mahupun $A_1$ tidak kosong
examples.suggested: setiap vektor ini hanya ditakrifkan apabila set yang sepadan dengannya tidak kosong, tetapi mulai sekarang kita akan fokus pada kes di mana kedua-dua $A_0$ dan $A_1$ tidak kosong
examples.why: 'bersamaan' means equal or equivalent, not corresponding. The bare 'A_0 mahupun A_1 tidak kosong' is less clear than stating outright that both sets are non-empty.

examples.source: verify that this expression agrees with the definition of $Z_{\mathrm{OR}}$
examples.translation: mengesahkan bahawa ungkapan ini bersetuju dengan definisi $Z_{\mathrm{OR}}$
examples.suggested: mengesahkan bahawa ungkapan ini sepadan dengan definisi $Z_{\mathrm{OR}}$
examples.why: 'bersetuju' means that a person agrees with something. It is a calque when used for mathematical consistency.

examples.source: this is a *reflection* about the line parallel to $\vert A_0\rangle$
examples.translation: ini adalah sebuah *pantulan* tentang garis yang selari dengan $\vert A_0\rangle$
examples.suggested: ini ialah *pantulan* terhadap garis yang selari dengan $\vert A_0\rangle$
examples.why: 'tentang' means 'concerning' and copies the English 'about'. Malay geometry says 'pantulan terhadap garis'. The same issue appears in [85].

examples.source: helpful for visualizing how the algorithm works
examples.translation: berguna untuk menvisualisasikan cara algoritma berfungsi
examples.suggested: berguna untuk memvisualisasikan cara algoritma berfungsi
examples.why: The prefix is spelled wrong. Before 'v', the meN- prefix becomes 'mem-'.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, including the harder last part: the 4/π² bound, the 1/4 bound and the repetition argument in [233] all match the English. There are some term slips. [10] renders "unitary quantum circuit" as "litar kuantum bersatu" ("united circuit"), while everywhere else in the file "unitary" is "uniter". Terms also drift: measurement "outcome" is "keputusan" in the first half and "hasil" in the second, "binary" is "binari" but becomes "perduaan" in [189], and "phase kickback" is "fasa kickback" in heading [8] but "phase kickback"/"phase kick-back" in the body. Smaller points are the calque "vektor eigenvector keadaan kuantum" in [13], "perbezaan" ("difference") used for "discrimination" in [74], "hasil darab dalam eksponen" in [153], which clashes with "hasil darab dalam" meaning inner product in [73]/[109], lowercase "get"/"litar" at the start of sentences, and "not immediately clear" losing "immediately" in [52].

examples.source: we have a unitary quantum circuit for the operation $U$
examples.translation: kita mempunyai litar kuantum bersatu untuk operasi $U$
examples.suggested: kita mempunyai litar kuantum uniter untuk operasi $U$
examples.why: 'bersatu' means united/unified, not unitary. Every other entry uses 'uniter', so this one hides the unitarity requirement.

examples.source: is the quantum state eigenvector of $U$
examples.translation: adalah vektor eigenvector keadaan kuantum bagi $U$
examples.suggested: ialah vektor eigen (keadaan kuantum) bagi $U$
examples.why: 'vektor eigenvector' says 'vector' twice. It is a stiff calque.

examples.source: and the measurements reveal $y$ (encoded in binary).
examples.translation: dan pengukuran mendedahkan $y$ (dikodkan dalam perduaan).
examples.suggested: dan pengukuran mendedahkan $y$ (dikodkan dalam binari).
examples.why: The rest of the file uses 'binari' (notasi binari, rentetan binari). Switching to 'perduaan' here is inconsistent. Measurement 'outcome' has the same problem, moving from 'keputusan' to 'hasil'.

examples.source: It can be checked by expanding the product in the exponent on the right-hand side,
examples.translation: Ia boleh disemak dengan mengembangkan hasil darab dalam eksponen pada bahagian kanan,
examples.suggested: Ia boleh disemak dengan mengembangkan hasil darab di dalam eksponen pada bahagian kanan,
examples.why: In this file 'hasil darab dalam' means inner product ([73], [109]), so this sentence can be misread as 'inner product exponent'. 'di dalam' removes the ambiguity.

examples.source: To perform such a discrimination with a quantum circuit
examples.translation: Untuk melaksanakan perbezaan sedemikian dengan litar kuantum
examples.suggested: Untuk melaksanakan pembezaan (diskriminasi) sedemikian dengan litar kuantum
examples.why: 'perbezaan' means difference, not the act of telling states apart.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. No entry would mislead a learner: the parity argument in [11], the phase kickback explanation in [30] and the XOR-versus-subtraction exponent point in [33] all come through correctly, and the core terms stay consistent (gerbang, litar, qubit, tendangan fasa, vektor eigen/nilai eigen). A native editor would still fix a few wording slips. "exclusive-OR" becomes the redundant "XOR eksklusif" ([10]). "humble origins" becomes "rendah hati" ([13]), which describes a person's modesty, not small beginnings. [3] uses the odd coinage "tatanomenklatur" where "tatanama" is standard. "define" is rendered two ways, "mendefinisikan" in [55] and "ditakrifkan/takrifkan" in [58] and [62].

examples.source: the parity (or, equivalently, the exclusive-OR) of the two bits
examples.translation: pariti (atau, secara setara, XOR eksklusif) dua bit tersebut
examples.suggested: pariti (atau, secara setara, OR eksklusif / XOR) dua bit tersebut
examples.why: 'XOR eksklusif' says 'exclusive' twice, because XOR already means exclusive-OR.

examples.source: Scientific advances sometimes have seemingly humble origins.
examples.translation: Kemajuan saintifik kadangkala mempunyai asal-usul yang kelihatan rendah hati.
examples.suggested: Kemajuan saintifik kadangkala bermula daripada sesuatu yang kelihatan kecil dan sederhana.
examples.why: 'rendah hati' means a person is modest, so applying it to origins is a literal calque.

examples.source: we'll follow that nomenclature in this lesson
examples.translation: kita akan menggunakan tatanomenklatur itu dalam pelajaran ini
examples.suggested: kita akan menggunakan tatanama itu dalam pelajaran ini
examples.why: 'tatanomenklatur' is a nonstandard hybrid. The standard Malay word is 'tatanama' (or 'nomenklatur').

examples.source: First we'll define a quantum circuit
examples.translation: Pertama kita akan mendefinisikan litar kuantum
examples.suggested: Pertama, kita akan mentakrifkan litar kuantum
examples.why: Entries [58], [61] and [62] use 'takrif' for 'define', so 'mendefinisikan' here is inconsistent within the file.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The coordinates, the polar and azimuthal angles, the Earth analogy, the antipodal points and the Bloch ball are all rendered correctly, and core terms stay consistent (matriks ketumpatan, keadaan tulen, gabungan cembung, sfera Bloch). Four English calques would still get changed by a native editor: "In words" becomes "Dalam kata-kata" (entries 21, 37, 43), "Along similar lines" becomes "Sepanjang garis yang sama" (31), and "unit 2-sphere" keeps English word order as "unit $2$-sfera" (23 onward). Entry 7 also renders "neither α nor β is zero" as "jika α mahupun β tidak sifar", which is grammatical but less clear than "kedua-dua α dan β bukan sifar".

examples.source: In words, thinking about a sphere as the planet Earth, ...
examples.translation: Dalam kata-kata, bayangkan sfera sebagai planet Bumi, ...
examples.suggested: Dengan kata lain, jika kita bayangkan sfera sebagai planet Bumi, ...
examples.why: 'Dalam kata-kata' copies 'In words' word for word. Malay would say 'Dengan kata lain' or 'Secara ringkasnya'. The same phrase also appears in entries 37 and 43.

examples.source: Along similar lines, the density matrix for the state |1> can be written like so.
examples.translation: Sepanjang garis yang sama, matriks ketumpatan untuk keadaan $\vert 1\rangle$ boleh ditulis seperti ini.
examples.suggested: Dengan cara yang sama, matriks ketumpatan untuk keadaan $\vert 1\rangle$ boleh ditulis seperti ini.
examples.why: This is a literal calque of the English idiom. In Malay it reads as if it were about geometric lines.

examples.source: If, however, neither α nor β is zero, then there's a unique choice ...
examples.translation: Namun, jika $\alpha$ mahupun $\beta$ tidak sifar, maka terdapat pilihan unik ...
examples.suggested: Namun, jika kedua-dua $\alpha$ dan $\beta$ bukan sifar, maka terdapat pilihan unik ...
examples.why: The 'X mahupun Y tidak' construction is grammatical, but a reader could take it as 'either α or β is non-zero'. Saying 'both are non-zero' outright removes that doubt.

examples.source: This sphere is typically called the unit 2-sphere
examples.translation: Sfera ini biasanya dipanggil *unit $2$-sfera*
examples.suggested: Sfera ini biasanya dipanggil *sfera-$2$ unit*
examples.why: 'unit 2-sfera' keeps the English modifier-first order. Malay puts the head noun first, as in 'sfera-2 unit'. The same form appears in entries 24, 28, 36 and 42.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. The main problem is terminology: "positive semidefinite" is rendered as "separa positif tertentu" in [67], where "tertentu" means "specific", not "definite". The Malay term is "separa tentu positif". "Probabilistic" is rendered consistently as "berkemungkinan" (which leans towards "likely"), where "berkebarangkalian" or "probabilistik" would be more precise. There are also a few calques: "bersetuju dengan bilangan" for "agrees with the number" [61], "Dalam kata-kata" for "In words" [63] and "mereka" used for states [16]. "Exactly" is dropped in [25] and [45].

examples.source: because $\rho$ is positive semidefinite
examples.translation: kerana $\rho$ adalah separa positif tertentu
examples.suggested: kerana $\rho$ adalah separa tentu positif
examples.why: 'tertentu' means 'specific/certain', not 'definite'. The conventional Malay term for positive semidefinite is 'separa tentu positif'.

examples.source: choose the number $m$ so that it agrees with the number of classical states
examples.translation: memilih nombor $m$ supaya ia bersetuju dengan bilangan keadaan klasikal
examples.suggested: memilih nombor $m$ supaya ia sama dengan bilangan keadaan klasikal
examples.why: 'bersetuju' means consenting or agreeing to something, which is a calque here. The mathematical sense is 'sama dengan'.

examples.source: In words, normal matrices are matrices that commute with their own conjugate transpose.
examples.translation: Dalam kata-kata, matriks normal adalah matriks yang bertukar ganti dengan transpos konjugat sendirinya.
examples.suggested: Dengan kata lain, matriks normal ialah matriks yang kalis tukar tertib dengan transpos konjugatnya sendiri.
examples.why: 'Dalam kata-kata' is a literal calque of 'In words'. The idiomatic phrase is 'Dengan kata lain'.

examples.source: Probabilistic selections of density matrices
examples.translation: Pemilihan berkemungkinan matriks ketumpatan
examples.suggested: Pemilihan berkebarangkalian matriks ketumpatan
examples.why: 'berkemungkinan' suggests 'likely/possible' rather than 'governed by probability'. It is used consistently across the file, so this is minor.

examples.source: We do in fact obtain exactly the same state either way.
examples.translation: Kita memang mendapatkan keadaan yang sama dalam kedua-dua cara.
examples.suggested: Kita memang mendapat keadaan yang betul-betul sama dalam kedua-dua cara.
examples.why: This drops 'exactly', which carries the emphasis. The same happens in [45] ('statistik output yang sama').

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The main defect is that 'positive semidefinite' is rendered two ways: as 'separuh-tentu positif' in the first half ([26], [27], [33], [39], [47], [66]) and as 'semidefinit positif' from [71] on ([94], [100], [108], [129]). 'Equality' is also split: 'persamaan kedua/ketiga' in [20] but 'kesamaan' in [98] and [105], and 'persamaan' is used for 'equation' elsewhere. A few calqued phrasings would read better rewritten natively: 'Kita juga mempunyai bahawa' ([16], [47]), 'kebarangkalian dengan mana' ([120]) and 'menetapkan bahawa ini memang kes demikian' ([32]).

examples.source: The first property is that they're all positive semidefinite matrices.
examples.translation: Sifat pertama ialah ia semua adalah matriks semidefinit positif.
examples.suggested: Sifat pertama ialah kesemuanya matriks separuh-tentu positif.
examples.why: Earlier entries ([26], [33], [47]) use 'separuh-tentu positif'. The second half switches to 'semidefinit positif', so a core term is inconsistent within the page.

examples.source: The last equality follows from the fact that $\Phi$ is a channel
examples.translation: Kesamaan terakhir mengikut dari fakta bahawa $\Phi$ ialah saluran
examples.suggested: Kesamaan terakhir terhasil daripada fakta bahawa $\Phi$ ialah saluran
examples.why: [20] renders 'equality' as 'persamaan', but here it is 'kesamaan'. 'mengikut dari' is also a calque of 'follows from'.

examples.source: so the probabilities with which different measurement outcomes are obtained can depend only on $\rho_{\mathsf{X}}$
examples.translation: jadi kebarangkalian dengan mana hasil pengukuran yang berbeza diperoleh hanya boleh bergantung pada $\rho_{\mathsf{X}}$
examples.suggested: jadi kebarangkalian untuk memperoleh setiap hasil pengukuran hanya boleh bergantung pada $\rho_{\mathsf{X}}$
examples.why: 'dengan mana' copies the English relative clause 'with which' and is not natural Malay.

examples.source: The following two observations establish that this is the case.
examples.translation: Dua pemerhatian berikut menetapkan bahawa ini memang kes demikian.
examples.suggested: Dua pemerhatian berikut membuktikan bahawa hal ini benar.
examples.why: 'menetapkan ... kes demikian' is a literal rendering of 'establish ... the case' and reads stiffly.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The existence proof, Schmidt decomposition, unitary equivalence, bit-commitment and HJW arguments keep their conditions and quantifiers, and I found no drift. The problems are consistency and calques. 'Reduced state' is 'keadaan teraruh' (which reads as 'induced state') in [61]-[90] but 'keadaan terturun' in [111] and [132]. 'Standard basis' is 'asas piawai' in [51] and [55] but 'asas standard' in [135] and [145]. There are also English calques: 'agree with' as 'bersetuju dengan' ([68], [89], [90]), 'it follows that' as 'ia mengikut bahawa' ([70], [84], [94]) and 'reasoning about' as 'membuat alasan' ([41]), where 'alasan' means 'excuse'.

examples.source: the reduced state of Bob's qubit B is the completely mixed state
examples.translation: keadaan terturun qubit Bob B ialah keadaan bercampur penuh
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering for 'reduced state' across the file, preferably 'keadaan terturun', and replace 'keadaan teraruh' in [61], [74], [86]-[90].
examples.why: The same concept appears under two names, and 'teraruh' suggests 'induced' rather than 'reduced'.

examples.source: the eigenvalues of the reduced states must agree with the squares of the Schmidt coefficients
examples.translation: nilai eigen keadaan teraruh mestilah bersetuju dengan kuasa dua pekali-pekali Schmidt
examples.suggested: nilai eigen keadaan terturun mestilah sama dengan kuasa dua pekali Schmidt
examples.why: 'bersetuju' means to consent, a calque of 'agree'. Mathematical agreement is 'sama dengan' or 'sepadan dengan'.

examples.source: when reasoning about a given quantum state vector
examples.translation: apabila membuat alasan tentang vektor keadaan kuantum
examples.suggested: apabila menaakul tentang vektor keadaan kuantum
examples.why: 'membuat alasan' means 'making excuses'. 'menaakul' is the right word for reasoning.

examples.source: a standard basis measurement performed on Z
examples.translation: pengukuran asas standard yang dilakukan pada Z
examples.suggested: pengukuran asas piawai yang dilakukan pada Z
examples.why: The file uses 'asas piawai' earlier ([51], [55]), so this term is inconsistent.

examples.source: is linearly independent, and so it follows that
examples.translation: adalah bebas linear, dan oleh itu ia mengikut bahawa
examples.suggested: adalah bebas linear, dan oleh itu
examples.why: 'ia mengikut bahawa' copies the English 'it follows that'. Plain 'maka' or 'oleh itu' is the natural Malay.

editor_note: I found no semantic drift. The cycle of implications, the non-uniqueness caveat, the N ≤ nm remark and the Gram-Schmidt step all carry the English meaning faithfully. Several math terms are imperfect, though. "Multiplicity" becomes "kepelbagaian" (diversity) instead of the standard "kegandaan". "Bilinearity" becomes the awkward "kelinearan dwi" instead of "kedwilinearan". "State discrimination" becomes "pembezaan keadaan", which reads like calculus differentiation. The page also spells the same root two ways ("ortogon" but "orthogonalisasi"), and has a few calques such as "Itulah kes di sini".

examples.source: eigenvalues with multiplicity larger than one
examples.translation: nilai-nilai eigen dengan kepelbagaian lebih daripada satu
examples.suggested: nilai-nilai eigen dengan kegandaan lebih daripada satu
examples.why: In Malay mathematics, eigenvalue multiplicity is 'kegandaan'. 'Kepelbagaian' means variety or diversity.

examples.source: together with the bilinearity of tensor products
examples.translation: bersama-sama dengan kelinearan dwi hasil darab tensor
examples.suggested: bersama-sama dengan sifat kedwilinearan hasil darab tensor
examples.why: 'Kelinearan dwi' is a word-by-word calque. The conventional form is 'kedwilinearan'.

examples.source: the Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization process ... the state discrimination problem
examples.translation: proses orthogonalisasi Gram-Schmidt ... masalah pembezaan keadaan
examples.suggested: proses pengortogonan (ortogonalisasi) Gram-Schmidt ... masalah diskriminasi keadaan
examples.why: 'Orthogonalisasi' keeps the English spelling, while entry 39 uses 'ortogon'. 'Pembezaan' is the usual word for calculus differentiation, so it is a confusing choice here.

examples.source: That is the case here
examples.translation: Itulah kes di sini
examples.suggested: Begitulah halnya di sini
examples.why: A literal calque of the English idiom. A native writer would not phrase it this way.

editor_note: Overall the meaning is faithful and nothing here would mislead a learner, but there are several calques and wrong word choices. "Disruptive" is rendered literally as "mengganggu" ("annoying/interfering") in [21] and [55]. Other literal renderings are "jiran di bawah jalan" ("under the road") in [64], "Pengambilan utama" for Key takeaways in [69] and "Kami tahu dalam diri kami" in [55]. Some terms are also off: "verification and validation" becomes a duplicated "pengesahan dan pengesahan" in [50], "thermodynamic observables" becomes "pemerhatian" ("observations") in [55], chip "area" becomes "kawasan" in [51], "energy-dense" becomes "bertenaga lebih tinggi" in [50], and "staffing" becomes "penggajian" in [21]. Terms are inconsistent too: "net-zero" is left in English in [65] but is "sifar bersih" in [33] and [63], and "baharu" and "baru" are mixed. There are typos or non-words: "penjuang" in [80] and "penyahjeteraan karbon" in [64].

examples.source: it has the potential to offer a disruptive solution for a core business problem
examples.translation: ia berpotensi menawarkan penyelesaian yang mengganggu
examples.suggested: ia berpotensi menawarkan penyelesaian revolusioner/transformatif
examples.why: 'mengganggu' means disturbing or annoying, so the business sense of 'disruptive' (game-changing) is lost. [55] 'benar-benar mengganggu' has the same problem.

examples.source: can you sell that excess energy to your neighbors down the road?
examples.translation: bolehkah anda menjual lebihan tenaga itu kepada jiran di bawah jalan?
examples.suggested: bolehkah anda menjual lebihan tenaga itu kepada jiran di hujung jalan?
examples.why: This is a literal calque that reads as 'neighbours under the road'. In the same entry, 'mencolok' should be 'mencucuk/memasang palam', and 'penyahjeteraan karbon' should be 'penyahkarbonan'.

examples.source: software verification and validation ... more energy-dense battery technologies
examples.translation: pengesahan dan pengesahan perisian ... teknologi bateri bertenaga lebih tinggi
examples.suggested: verifikasi dan validasi perisian ... teknologi bateri berketumpatan tenaga lebih tinggi
examples.why: The duplicated word erases the distinction between verification and validation. 'Bertenaga lebih tinggi' suggests higher power, not higher energy density.

examples.source: accurately calculate thermodynamic observables
examples.translation: mengira secara tepat pemerhatian termodinamik
examples.suggested: mengira secara tepat cerapan (observable) termodinamik
examples.why: 'Pemerhatian' means 'observations', not the physical-quantity sense of 'observable'. The term is still recognizable but imprecise.

examples.source: Key takeaways
examples.translation: Pengambilan utama
examples.suggested: Rumusan utama
examples.why: 'Pengambilan' means intake/uptake. This is a word-for-word calque of 'takeaways'.

examples.source: identifying a quantum computing champion
examples.translation: mengenal pasti penjuang pengkomputeran kuantum
examples.suggested: mengenal pasti peneraju/penggerak pengkomputeran kuantum
examples.why: 'penjuang' is a typo for 'pejuang', and 'champion' here means an internal advocate, not a fighter. 'quantum ready' is also left in English.

editor_note: Overall the translation is faithful, and the core terms are mostly consistent: litar variasi, pembelitan, get, nilai jangkaan, tenaga keadaan dasar. Entry [13] breaks that consistency by leaving "gate" and "entanglement" in English, where the rest of the file uses "get" and "pembelitan". It also uses lowercase "anda" instead of the "Anda" used elsewhere. In [12], SU(2) is glossed as "kumpulan perpaduan khas", which is a literal calque of the source's "unity" slip; "perpaduan" means social solidarity, and the correct term is "kumpulan unitari khas". There are also two hedge problems: [31] renders "not likely to" as "tidak mungkin", which can read as "impossible", and [29] calques "In all likelihood" as "Dalam semua kemungkinan".

examples.source: special unity group of degree 2
examples.translation: kumpulan perpaduan khas berdarjah 2
examples.suggested: kumpulan unitari khas berdarjah 2
examples.why: 'Perpaduan' means social unity or solidarity. SU(2) is the special unitary group, so the correct math term is 'unitari'.

examples.source: two types of SU(2) gates ... entanglement scheme ... If you simply
examples.translation: dua jenis gate SU(2) ... skema entanglement ... Jika anda hanya
examples.suggested: dua jenis get SU(2) ... skema pembelitan ... Jika Anda hanya
examples.why: The rest of the file uses 'get' and 'pembelitan', and it capitalizes 'Anda'.

examples.source: is not likely to yield a substantially better match
examples.translation: tidak mungkin menghasilkan padanan yang jauh lebih baik
examples.suggested: tidak berkemungkinan menghasilkan padanan yang jauh lebih baik
examples.why: 'Tidak mungkin' usually reads as 'impossible', which makes the English hedge stronger than intended.

examples.source: In all likelihood, the last qubit should either be entangled
examples.translation: Dalam semua kemungkinan, qubit terakhir sama ada perlu dibelit
examples.suggested: Besar kemungkinan, qubit terakhir sama ada perlu dibelit
examples.why: 'Dalam semua kemungkinan' is a word-for-word calque of the English idiom. 'Besar kemungkinan' is the natural Malay phrase.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner, but a few spots need fixing. "Optimizer" is translated as "pengoptimum" everywhere except [17], which switches to "optimizer klasik" and "minimizer tempatan" and refers to the algorithms as "mereka", a pronoun meant for people. In [12], "fit into a VQE calculation" becomes "sesuai dalam", which means "suitable in" rather than "what role they play". In [18], "a different stopping criterion" loses "different". In [6], "dalam kehadiran dan ketiadaan hingar" is a stiff word-for-word copy of the English "in the presence and absence of noise".

examples.source: Most available classical optimization algorithms are local minimizers ... Some classical optimizers explicitly estimate gradients
examples.translation: adalah minimizer tempatan, dalam erti kata mereka menggunakan ... Sesetengah optimizer klasik secara eksplisit
examples.suggested: adalah peminimum setempat, iaitu ia menggunakan ... Sesetengah pengoptimum klasik secara eksplisit
examples.why: The rest of the file uses 'pengoptimum', and the algorithms should be 'ia', not 'mereka'.

examples.source: How classical optimizers fit into a VQE calculation
examples.translation: Bagaimana pengoptimum klasik sesuai dalam pengiraan VQE
examples.suggested: Peranan pengoptimum klasik dalam pengiraan VQE
examples.why: 'sesuai' means 'suitable', which misses the sense of 'fit into' (the optimizer's place in the workflow).

examples.source: All have some option specifying a different stopping criterion based on function or variable values
examples.translation: Kesemuanya mempunyai pilihan tertentu untuk menentukan kriteria penghentian berdasarkan nilai fungsi atau pembolehubah
examples.suggested: Kesemuanya mempunyai pilihan untuk menentukan kriteria penghentian lain berdasarkan nilai fungsi atau pembolehubah
examples.why: The translation drops 'different', i.e. that this is a criterion in addition to maxiter.

examples.source: how they perform in the presence and absence of noise
examples.translation: bagaimana prestasinya dalam kehadiran dan ketiadaan hingar
examples.suggested: bagaimana prestasinya apabila terdapat hingar dan tanpa hingar
examples.why: This copies the English phrasing word for word and reads stiffly in Malay.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The key claims keep their original force: in [24], extra optimizer steps are "tidak mungkin" to help, and in [27], hardware is closer because only it used error mitigation. The remaining problems are small. In [18], "total energy" is calqued as "tenaga jumlah", while [27] correctly uses "jumlah tenaga". "Fermionic" is left as the English "fermionic" in [7] and [10] instead of the Malay "fermionik". In [25], "julat nilai yang sedikit berbeza yang diambil sampel" is a stiff stack of relative clauses.

examples.source: we store both the total energy and the electronic energy
examples.translation: kita simpan kedua-dua tenaga jumlah dan tenaga elektronik
examples.suggested: kita simpan kedua-dua jumlah tenaga dan tenaga elektronik
examples.why: 'tenaga jumlah' copies English word order. Malay says 'jumlah tenaga', and the file itself uses that form in [27].

examples.source: it starts in the fermionic Hamiltonian construction
examples.translation: ia bermula dalam pembinaan Hamiltonian fermionic
examples.suggested: ia bermula dalam pembinaan Hamiltonian fermionik
examples.why: The English adjective is left untranslated. The standard Malay spelling is 'fermionik' (like 'elektronik'). The same fix applies to [10].

examples.source: aside from a slightly different range of values sampled
examples.translation: selain julat nilai yang sedikit berbeza yang diambil sampel
examples.suggested: kecuali julat nilai yang disampel sedikit berbeza
examples.why: Two 'yang' clauses in a row make the sentence read like machine translation. A single restructured clause is more natural.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and I found nothing that would mislead a learner, but a few spots need fixing. 'fermionic' stays in English throughout ('Hamiltonian fermionic', 'operator fermionic'), yet 'bosonic' becomes Malay 'bosonik', so the paired terms don't match. 'Total energy' is rendered as both the calqued 'tenaga jumlah' ([32], [35]) and the natural 'jumlah tenaga' ([32]). Two word choices are off: 'fitting' Slater-type orbitals becomes 'pemasangan' ([28]), which means installation, and 'identical fermions' becomes 'fermion yang serupa' ([12]), which means similar. In [42], 'subject to antisymmetry' is weakened to 'sesuai dengan antisimetri'.

examples.source: named for fitting Slater-Type Orbitals using 6 primitive Gaussian orbitals
examples.translation: dinamakan sempena pemasangan Orbital Jenis Slater
examples.suggested: dinamakan sempena penyuaian Orbital Jenis Slater
examples.why: 'pemasangan' means installation or mounting, not curve or function fitting.

examples.source: specific to systems of identical fermions
examples.translation: untuk sistem fermion yang serupa
examples.suggested: untuk sistem fermion yang identik
examples.why: 'serupa' means similar. The physics depends on the particles being truly identical (indistinguishable).

examples.source: and correspondingly subject to antisymmetry under exchange
examples.translation: dan sesuai dengan antisimetri di bawah pertukaran
examples.suggested: dan oleh itu tertakluk kepada antisimetri di bawah pertukaran
examples.why: 'sesuai dengan' means 'consistent with' or 'suitable for'. That loses the point that the system is bound by antisymmetry as a consequence.

examples.source: one can describe total energy ... total electronic orbital energy
examples.translation: tenaga jumlah ... tenaga orbital elektronik jumlah
examples.suggested: jumlah tenaga ... jumlah tenaga orbital elektronik
examples.why: 'tenaga jumlah' is a calque of the English word order. The same entry later uses the natural 'jumlah tenaga', so the term is also inconsistent.

examples.source: Generate the fermionic Hamiltonian
examples.translation: Jana Hamiltonian fermionic
examples.suggested: Jana Hamiltonian fermionik
examples.why: 'fermionic' is left in English while 'bosonic' becomes 'bosonik'. Using 'fermionik' would make the pair consistent.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through and nothing would mislead a learner. The time estimates (6-10 hours, two hours of video and reading), Dr. Lipinska's title and the four Qiskit patterns steps all match the English. A native editor would still smooth three spots of English word order carried over into Malay: "Dalam menetapkan pengiraan VQE" [7], "Proses pasca" as the post-processing step [11], and "Kami mengesyorkan merancang untuk meluangkan" [13]. Terminology is consistent: pengoptimum klasik, primitif, keadaan dasar, and variational quantum eigensolver kept in English.

examples.source: In setting up a VQE calculation, we will follow the standard Qiskit patterns framework:
examples.translation: Dalam menetapkan pengiraan VQE, kita akan mengikuti rangka kerja corak Qiskit standard:
examples.suggested: Semasa menyediakan pengiraan VQE, kita akan mengikuti rangka kerja corak Qiskit yang standard:
examples.why: 'Dalam menetapkan' copies the English 'In setting up'. 'Semasa menyediakan' is the natural Malay way to say it.

examples.source: Post-process, return result in classical format
examples.translation: Proses pasca, kembalikan hasil dalam format klasik
examples.suggested: Lakukan pasca-pemprosesan, kembalikan hasil dalam format klasik
examples.why: 'Proses pasca' reverses the usual word order and doesn't read as an instruction like the other patterns steps (Petakan, Optimumkan, Laksanakan).

examples.source: We recommend planning to devote approximately 6-10 hours to the completion of this course.
examples.translation: Kami mengesyorkan merancang untuk meluangkan kira-kira 6-10 jam untuk menyelesaikan kursus ini.
examples.suggested: Kami mengesyorkan anda memperuntukkan kira-kira 6-10 jam untuk menyelesaikan kursus ini.
examples.why: 'mengesyorkan merancang untuk meluangkan' strings three verbs together, copying the English. It reads as stiff and word-for-word.

editor_note: The course's central term, "diagonalization", has two renderings. Entries [0] and [7] use the correct "pepenjuruan". Entries [5], [6], [8], [11], [12], [21], [25], [26] and [28] use "penepatan", which means "placement/fixing", not diagonalization. So the course title becomes "Algoritma Penepatan Kuantum" ("Quantum Placement Algorithms"), and a learner would get the wrong idea of what the course is about. There are also two minor calques: "matriks minat kita" in [7] (for "our matrix of interest") and "rakan sejawat kuantum mereka" in [12] (for "their quantum counterparts").

examples.source: Welcome to Quantum Diagonalization Algorithms!
examples.translation: Selamat datang ke Algoritma Penepatan Kuantum!
examples.suggested: Selamat datang ke Algoritma Pepenjuruan Kuantum!
examples.why: 'Penepatan' means placement/fixing, so a learner would take the course to be about placing something rather than diagonalizing a matrix. Entries [0] and [7] already use the correct term 'pepenjuruan'.

examples.source: can be cast as matrix diagonalization problems
examples.translation: boleh dirumuskan sebagai masalah penepatan matriks
examples.suggested: boleh dirumuskan sebagai masalah pepenjuruan matriks
examples.why: 'Masalah penepatan matriks' reads as 'matrix placement problem', which is not what the English says. The same wrong term appears in [8], [11], [12], [21], [25], [26] and [28].

examples.source: suitable subspaces in which to project our matrix of interest
examples.translation: subruang yang sesuai untuk memproyeksikan matriks minat kita
examples.suggested: subruang yang sesuai untuk memproyeksikan matriks yang kita kaji
examples.why: 'Matriks minat kita' is a word-for-word calque of 'matrix of interest' and does not read naturally in Malay.

examples.source: classical diagonalization approaches and their quantum counterparts
examples.translation: pendekatan penepatan klasik dan rakan sejawat kuantum mereka
examples.suggested: pendekatan pepenjuruan klasik dan padanan kuantumnya
examples.why: 'Rakan sejawat' means a human colleague, and 'mereka' is a pronoun for people. For methods, 'padanan' is the natural word.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. That covers the 0.90^10 ≈ 35% worked answer, the (1-p)^N scaling caveat, the claim that the kernel dimension depends on training points and not features, and the 60-vs-77 depth comparison. "Error mitigation" appears as "pengurangan ralat" in [16], [25], [52] and [71] but as "mitigasi ralat" in [58], so the file is inconsistent. Several phrases are calques a native editor would rewrite: '"kuasi-kebarangkalian" yang dipanggil' for "so-called" ([16]), "Seseorang dapat melihat" for "One sees" ([45]), "antara alat lain" for "among other tools" ([52]) and "kawasan penyelidikan" where Malay says "bidang penyelidikan" ([93]). A few renderings also shift the tone slightly. "Non-starter" becomes "mustahil" (impossible) in [82], and "intractably high" becomes "tidak dapat diterima" (unacceptable) in [68].

examples.source: and they do not use error mitigation
examples.translation: dan mereka tidak menggunakan mitigasi ralat
examples.suggested: dan mereka tidak menggunakan pengurangan ralat
examples.why: Everywhere else in the file (entries 16, 25, 52, 71), 'error mitigation' is 'pengurangan ralat'. Using a different term here splits the concept.

examples.source: (or so-called "quasi-probabilities", if certain error mitigation methods are used)
examples.translation: (atau "kuasi-kebarangkalian" yang dipanggil, jika kaedah pengurangan ralat tertentu digunakan)
examples.suggested: (atau yang dipanggil "kuasi-kebarangkalian", jika kaedah pengurangan ralat tertentu digunakan)
examples.why: Putting 'yang dipanggil' after the term is a calque and reads awkwardly. Natural Malay puts it before the term, or uses 'apa yang dikenali sebagai'.

examples.source: But a two-qubit depth of more than 100, even before transpilation is a non-starter.
examples.translation: Tetapi kedalaman dua-qubit melebihi 100, bahkan sebelum transpilasi, adalah mustahil.
examples.suggested: Tetapi kedalaman dua-qubit melebihi 100, bahkan sebelum transpilasi, memang tidak praktikal.
examples.why: 'Mustahil' (impossible) makes the claim stronger than the English. 'Non-starter' means impractical, not physically impossible.

examples.source: One sees that for a large number of qubits, pictures like this quickly become intractable.
examples.translation: Seseorang dapat melihat bahawa untuk bilangan qubit yang besar, gambar seperti ini dengan cepat menjadi tidak mudah difahami.
examples.suggested: Dapat dilihat bahawa untuk bilangan qubit yang besar, gambar rajah seperti ini cepat menjadi sukar ditafsir.
examples.why: 'Seseorang dapat melihat' carries over the English impersonal 'one' word for word. Malay technical writing would use the passive 'Dapat dilihat'.

examples.source: is an area of current research
examples.translation: adalah kawasan penyelidikan semasa
examples.suggested: merupakan bidang penyelidikan semasa
examples.why: 'Kawasan' means a geographic area. The standard Malay for a research field is 'bidang'.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, but a few entries need fixing. In [76], quantum "noise" is rendered as "bunyi" ("sound"). The established Malay term is "hingar", and [21] already uses "bising", so the concept is also inconsistent across the file. In [41], "computationally intractable" became "tidak dapat dikira secara pengiraan", which repeats itself and reads as "uncomputable", a stronger claim than the English "intractable". In [22], "It is unlikely" became "Adalah tidak mungkin", which usually reads as "impossible"; the next sentence ("kita meramalkan...") softens this, but it should be hedged. There are also calques in [4] ("Dengan fikiran itu", "apa yang pengkomputeran kuantum bukan") and [25] ("memproses hasil selepas").

examples.source: quantum models must contend with issues such as data loading, noise, and scaling
examples.translation: model kuantum mesti bersaing dengan isu seperti pemuatan data, bunyi, dan penskalaan
examples.suggested: model kuantum perlu menangani isu seperti pemuatan data, hingar, dan penskalaan
examples.why: 'bunyi' means acoustic sound. Quantum noise is 'hingar', and [21] uses 'bising', so the file is inconsistent. 'bersaing dengan' is also a literal calque of 'contend with'.

examples.source: often become computationally intractable as the problem size grows
examples.translation: sering menjadi tidak dapat dikira secara pengiraan apabila saiz masalah meningkat
examples.suggested: sering menjadi sukar dikendalikan secara pengiraan apabila saiz masalah meningkat
examples.why: The rendering repeats itself and suggests 'uncomputable', which is not the same as 'intractable' (too costly to solve in practice).

examples.source: It is unlikely that error correction will completely replace error mitigation.
examples.translation: Adalah tidak mungkin bahawa pembetulan ralat akan menggantikan sepenuhnya pengurangan ralat.
examples.suggested: Kemungkinan besar pembetulan ralat tidak akan menggantikan sepenuhnya pengurangan ralat.
examples.why: 'tidak mungkin' normally reads as 'impossible', which strengthens the hedged English 'unlikely'.

examples.source: With that in mind, it is best to start with what quantum computing is not:
examples.translation: Dengan fikiran itu, lebih baik mulakan dengan apa yang pengkomputeran kuantum bukan:
examples.suggested: Oleh itu, lebih baik kita mulakan dengan perkara yang bukan pengkomputeran kuantum:
examples.why: Word-for-word calque of English syntax that a native technical writer would not use.

examples.source: scheduling jobs, and post-processing results
examples.translation: menjadualkan kerja, dan memproses hasil selepas
examples.suggested: menjadualkan kerja, dan melakukan pasca-pemprosesan hasil
examples.why: 'memproses hasil selepas' is awkward, and [62] already uses 'pasca-pemprosesan' for this concept.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The spin-swap passage in [87] keeps every detail: the transverse and longitudinal cases, the ±45° intermediate case, the 67% probability and the right-to-left label caveat. The core terms are consistent: litar, kedalaman litar, transpilasi, nilai jangkaan, Suzuki–Trotter peringkat kedua/keempat. There are some wording problems: "commute" is rendered "bertukar ganti", where Malay mathematics uses "berkalis tukar" (from kalis tukar, commutative). "Evolve our state" in [22] is rendered "mengembangkan keadaan", which clashes with "berevolusi" in [87] and with "pengembangan Taylor" (Taylor expansion). The word "primitive" is dropped in [60].

examples.source: When $H_1$ and $H_2$ commute, we have the familiar case
examples.translation: Apabila $H_1$ dan $H_2$ bertukar ganti, kita mempunyai kes biasa
examples.suggested: Apabila $H_1$ dan $H_2$ berkalis tukar, kita mempunyai kes biasa
examples.why: In Malay mathematics, commutativity is 'kalis tukar' (commutative law = hukum kalis tukar). 'Bertukar ganti' just means 'interchange'. A learner can still recognise it, but it is not the conventional term. It recurs in [13] and [19].

examples.source: we might need to evolve our state for a longer time
examples.translation: kita mungkin perlu mengembangkan keadaan kita untuk masa yang lebih lama
examples.suggested: kita mungkin perlu membiarkan keadaan kita berevolusi untuk masa yang lebih lama
examples.why: 'Mengembangkan' reads as 'expand/develop' and shares a root with 'pengembangan Taylor' (Taylor expansion) two entries earlier. [87] uses 'berevolusi' for the same idea.

examples.source: Qiskit's `StatevectorEstimator` (EstimatorV2) primitive estimates expectation values of observables
examples.translation: `StatevectorEstimator` (EstimatorV2) Qiskit menganggar nilai jangkaan bagi kuantiti boleh cerap (observable)
examples.suggested: Primitif `StatevectorEstimator` (EstimatorV2) Qiskit menganggar nilai jangkaan bagi kuantiti boleh cerap (observable)
examples.why: The word 'primitive' is dropped. [95] keeps it ('Primitif `Sampler` (V2)'), so the two primitives are introduced unevenly.

examples.source: might become deprecated since these are static images
examples.translation: mungkin sudah lapuk kerana ianya imej statik
examples.suggested: mungkin sudah lapuk kerana ia merupakan imej statik
examples.why: 'Ianya' is a common but non-standard form. A careful Malay technical editor would write 'ia' instead.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The local/global trade-offs, the bootstrapping caveat and the barren-plateau scaling claim are all faithful. There are some word-sense slips. In [22], 'steepest descent' becomes 'keturunan paling curam', but 'keturunan' means lineage or ancestry, so it should be 'penurunan paling curam'. 'Noise' appears as 'bising'/'berbising' in [26]/[35] but as 'bunyi' (acoustic sound) in [36]. The coined adjective 'variasikal' for 'variational' is used consistently, but it is not standard Malay ('variasi' or 'variasional' is conventional). There are also smaller slips: capitalised 'Anda' in [39], and 'kawasan ini' in [33] for a research 'area', which should be 'bidang ini'.

examples.source: update the parameters towards the direction of steepest descent of the function
examples.translation: mengemas kini parameter ke arah keturunan paling curam fungsi tersebut
examples.suggested: mengemas kini parameter ke arah penurunan paling curam fungsi tersebut
examples.why: 'keturunan' means descent in the genealogical sense (lineage). The optimization term is 'penurunan'.

examples.source: This can reduce the impact of noise
examples.translation: Ini boleh mengurangkan kesan bunyi
examples.suggested: Ini boleh mengurangkan kesan hingar (or: kesan bising, matching [26]/[35])
examples.why: 'bunyi' means acoustic sound, not signal or quantum noise. It is also inconsistent with 'bising'/'berbising' elsewhere in this file.

examples.source: select the next set of parameters in a variational loop
examples.translation: memilih set parameter seterusnya dalam gelung variasikal
examples.suggested: memilih set parameter seterusnya dalam gelung variasi
examples.why: 'variasikal' is not a standard Malay word. It is used consistently, but 'variasi'/'variasional' is the conventional rendering.

examples.source: While this area is still under active research
examples.translation: Walaupun kawasan ini masih dalam penyelidikan aktif
examples.suggested: Walaupun bidang ini masih giat dikaji
examples.why: This is a calque: 'kawasan' is a physical area. A field of research is 'bidang'.

examples.source: With this lesson, you learned how to define your optimization loop:
examples.translation: Dengan pelajaran ini, Anda telah belajar cara menentukan gelung pengoptimuman:
examples.suggested: Dalam pelajaran ini, anda telah belajar cara menentukan gelung pengoptimuman anda:
examples.why: Capitalised 'Anda' mid-sentence is an Indonesian convention; standard Malay uses lowercase 'anda'. The possessive 'your' is also dropped.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The variational-theorem argument in [40]–[51] keeps its direction: expected energy is at least the ground-state energy, lower bounds must exist, upper bounds generally don't, and the ≥ reasoning carries over to upper bounds. The main term problem is "Trade-offs" in [6] and [53]. It is rendered "pertukaran", which reads as "exchange/change", where "tukar ganti" is the conventional term. In [24], "finalization criteria" is rendered "kriteria penyelesaian", which clashes with "penyelesaian" meaning "solution" in the same sentence, so "kriteria penamatan" is better. There are also smaller slips: "unitary" is left untranslated in [12] (should be "unitari"), "mereka" is used for non-human referents in [3] and [51], and the phrasing in [44] is stiff.

examples.source: Trade-offs associated with each step
examples.translation: Pertukaran yang berkaitan dengan setiap langkah
examples.suggested: Tukar ganti yang berkaitan dengan setiap langkah
examples.why: 'Pertukaran' means exchange or change, not a compromise between competing goals. The same rendering appears again in [53].

examples.source: until the classical optimizer's finalization criteria are met
examples.translation: sehingga kriteria penyelesaian pengoptimum klasik dipenuhi
examples.suggested: sehingga kriteria penamatan pengoptimum klasik dipenuhi
examples.why: 'Penyelesaian' is also used for 'solution' in the same sentence, so readers may take it as 'solution criteria' instead of stopping criteria.

examples.source: a unitary reference operator $U_R$
examples.translation: operator rujukan unitary $U_R$
examples.suggested: operator rujukan unitari $U_R$
examples.why: The English adjective is left untranslated. The standard Malay form is 'unitari'.

examples.source: making them ideal candidates to achieve quantum advantage
examples.translation: menjadikan mereka calon ideal untuk mencapai kelebihan kuantum
examples.suggested: menjadikannya calon yang ideal untuk mencapai kelebihan kuantum
examples.why: 'Mereka' is for people. Algorithms should take '-nya'. The same slip appears in [51] for observables.

examples.source: will be the closest that one can get to $\lambda_0$
examples.translation: adalah yang paling hampir yang boleh dicapai kepada $\lambda_0$
examples.suggested: ialah nilai yang paling hampir dengan $\lambda_0$ yang boleh dicapai
examples.why: This is calqued English syntax. 'Hampir ... kepada' is also an awkward collocation.
